# Omni View Africa & Middle East
> **About one hundred fifty people were on a Flydubai jet that sent a hijack code, and Israel scrambled fighters.**

**What You Need to Know:** About one hundred fifty people were on a Flydubai jet from Dubai toward Tel Aviv that sent a hijack code on Wednesday, and Israel scrambled fighters. An Israeli security official said there was no definitive information of a hijacking and that the pilot had activated a distress signal. October petrol in the Emirates rises for a third month, and Nigeria used a UN disarmament meeting to demand that nuclear arsenals be eliminated.

### Lead
**Dubai-Tel Aviv flight reports suspected hijacking; Israeli fighter jets scrambled: Ynetnews**
A Flydubai aircraft bound from Dubai to Tel Aviv, with about 150 people aboard, sent an emergency signal on Wednesday that indicated a possible hijacking, and Israel scrambled two fighter jets to escort it, Ynetnews reports. The alert came as the jet was descending manually and making a U-turn. It had left Dubai at 7:05 a.m. and was scheduled into Ben Gurion Airport near Tel Aviv at about 9:30 a.m. About 90 minutes out, entering Jordanian airspace, it transmitted squawk code 7700, the general-emergency code, then code 7500, used for unlawful interference including a possible hijacking. It turned back into Saudi airspace, flew lower, went south, then west, and stayed over the kingdom. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz convened an urgent security consultation.

### Across the Region
**UAE petrol prices to rise by about 16% in October: The National**
UAE petrol prices will rise in October for a third consecutive month, The National reports, with global crude still elevated and a US-Iran truce uncertain. Super 98 goes to Dh4.40 from Dh3.80, a 15.7 percent increase. Special 95 goes to Dh4.28 from Dh3.69, and E-Plus 91 to Dh4.21 from Dh3.61, rises of nearly 16 percent and 16.6 percent. Diesel goes to Dh4.80 from Dh4.30, up 11.6 percent. The National links the pump moves to September crude, when Brent neared $110 and West Texas Intermediate topped $105 after the United States and Iran resumed offensives and Yemen’s Houthis escalated attacks on Saudi facilities in the Red Sea; since early July, when UAE petrol last fell, Brent is up nearly 45 percent. Source: [thenationalnews.com](https://www.thenationalnews.com/business/energy/2026/09/30/uae-petrol-prices-to-rise-by-about-16-in-october/)

**Ghana’s minister calls LPG investments key to 2030 target: MyJoyOnline**
Ghana’s Minister of Energy and Green Transition, John Abdulai Jinapor, said sustained investment in liquefied petroleum gas infrastructure matters for the government’s goal of at least 50 percent LPG access by 2030, MyJoyOnline reported. He cited the commissioning of a 6,000-metric-ton LPG storage terminal and the first gas delivery by the vessel MT Asharami Ghana. He said projects of that kind should widen access to cleaner cooking fuel and harden energy security and the LPG supply chain. He praised Asharami Ghana and Sahara Group, and said the terminal could open work in trade, logistics, transportation and distribution. Source: [ua.news](https://ua.news/en/energetika/ministr-gani-nazvav-investitsiyi-u-zvg-kliuchovimi-dlia-meti-do-2030-roku-myjoyonline)

### Also Today
**Tanzania Removes Special Visa Clearance for Nigerians: AllAfrica**
Tanzania has removed Nigerian nationals from its referred visa category, ending the special clearance they needed before they could obtain visas, Vanguard reports. Source: [allafrica.com](https://allafrica.com/stories/202609300086.html)

**Araghchi receives US feedback on trust-building plan, set to discuss with Iranian leadership: Middle East Eye**
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi received US feedback in Doha late Tuesday, via Qatari mediators, on a seven-day trust-building plan, and will discuss that response with Tehran’s leadership on Wednesday, an official told Reuters. Source: [middleeasteye.net](https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/araghchi-receives-us-feedback-trust-building-plan-set-discuss-iranian)

**Burkina Faso Launches First Gold Refinery: AllAfrica**
Burkina Faso has launched its first gold refinery, and Mr Traore, in a government Information Service statement, said the country has reached a historic milestone in its quest for economic independence, Premium Times reports. Source: [allafrica.com](https://allafrica.com/stories/202609300060.html)

**2027 AFCON qualifiers: first win for Patrick Vieira and Senegal: France 24**
Patrick Vieira won his first match as Senegal’s manager,, France 24 reports. Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/sports/20260930-2027-afcon-qualifiers-first-win-for-patrick-vieira-and-senegal)

### The Region and the World
**Nigeria rejects nuclear deterrence, demands total elimination of atomic weapons: Realnews Magazine**
Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Jimoh Ibrahim, told a high-level UN meeting in New York on Tuesday that the only absolute guarantee against the use or threat of nuclear weapons is their total elimination. The session marked the International Day for the Total Elimination of Nuclear Weapons during the 81st General Assembly. He said Nigeria does not possess nuclear weapons, has never pursued a nuclear-weapons programme, has no intention of doing so, and does not rest its security on them. He said thousands of warheads remain while nuclear-weapon states continue modernisation programmes. He urged those states to honour Article VI of the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons and to eliminate their arsenals in a manner that is irreversible, transparent and verifiable. Source: [realnewsmagazine.net](https://realnewsmagazine.net/nigeria-rejects-nuclear-deterrence-demands-total-elimination-of-atomic-weapons/)

### Both Sides: Whether Nigeria should enlarge its budget while years still overlap
Nigeria has extended implementation of the 2025 capital budget to 31 December 2026. Minister of Budget and Economic Planning Senator Abubakar Bagudu has again called for a much larger national budget. The argument is whether spending should grow toward a one-trillion-dollar economy while budget years overlap and the revenue base stays narrow.

Bagudu’s case, as Arise News reports it, starts with scale. He argues that public spending at its present level cannot fund the infrastructure and development that a one-trillion-dollar economy requires, so the budget has to grow if that ambition is serious.

Dr Chijioke Ekechukwu, an economist and vice president of the Abuja Chamber of Commerce and Industry, starts with discipline. He told Arise News that budget overlaps give the impression Nigeria is not a very serious country and do not show fiscal discipline. A larger budget, he said, means larger expenditure, and expenditure has to be set against revenue. He put Nigeria’s revenue-to-GDP ratio at less than 10 percent. Without a wider revenue base, he argued, a bigger budget only widens the deficit and the borrowing that fills it. Investors watching from outside, he said, will ask whether a government that cannot hold a budget cycle should be taken seriously. What he wants next is a return to January-to-December, with capital and recurrent funds released so the spending falls inside the year.

The fact both are working from is the extension: the 2025 capital budget now runs through 31 December 2026. Ekechukwu’s test is whether money is released inside a normal financial year; the extension already on the books runs to the end of 2026. Source: [arise.tv](https://www.arise.tv/chijioke-ekechukwu-budget-overlaps-show-nigeria-is-not-a-serious-country/)

### Progress Watch
**Saudi Restarts Yanbu Oil Loadings After East-West Pipeline Reopens: Egypt Oil & Gas**
Saudi Arabia has resumed crude and refined-product loadings at the Red Sea port of Yanbu after restarting the East-West Pipeline, Egypt Oil & Gas reports, citing Reuters. The line was shut on 11 September after drone attacks that Saudi Arabia attributed to Iraqi militias, and operations resumed on 22 September. Saudi Aramco has notified customers of an October loading schedule from Yanbu, and tanker-tracking data showed loadings already under way. European Space Agency imagery from 27 September, read by TankerTrackers, indicated nearly 10 million barrels of crude being loaded at Yanbu and the nearby Al Muajjiz terminal. Industry sources put throughput near 2 million barrels a day and Kpler near 2.65 million; Kpler expects 3 million to 4 million barrels a day in the coming days, and says a return to the pre-attack level of about 5.5 million could take another month. Source: [egyptoil-gas.com](https://egyptoil-gas.com/news/saudi-restarts-yanbu-oil-loadings-after-east-west-pipeline-reopens/)

# Omni View Africa & Middle East
> **One-fifth of prewar oil traffic hinges on Tehran's Tuesday ask to reopen Hormuz.**

**What You Need to Know:** Iran says it expects Washington's answer on Tuesday to a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a route that carried a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas before the war. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says reopening depends on conditions Tehran has already sent, including a seven-day regional ceasefire and an end to the US naval blockade. Qatari intermediaries are carrying the ideas back to the American side.

### Lead
**Iran says it expects US response Tuesday on plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz: France 24**
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said late Monday that to Tehran's proposal to open the Strait of Hormuz, France 24 reported from state media. Qatari intermediaries had presented ideas and discussed them with Iran; they were to raise the matter with the American side once more, after which the final US response would be conveyed to Tehran. Araghchi, in New York for the UN General Assembly, said the Qataris hoped that would be done by Tuesday. He said the current focus is solely on the strait, and that reopening is contingent on conditions Iran has communicated. Before the war that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran in late February,; Tehran then imposed a blockade on Hormuz, and Washington answered with a blockade on Iranian ports. As a precondition for ending its blockade,, including in Lebanon, where its ally Hezbollah has been battling Israeli forces, plus the unfreezing of Iranian assets abroad, the lifting of sanctions on its oil sector, and an end to the US naval blockade. Last week in New York, Araghchi held discussions with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20260929-iran-says-expects-us-response-tuesday-plan-reopen-strait-of-hormuz)

### Across the Region
**Kenya: Court Halts Dangote Refinery Groundbreaking in Lamu: AllAfrica**
A Malindi Environment and Land Court has temporarily stopped planned construction of the Dangote refinery in Lamu County. Justice Jane Onyango certified as urgent a petition by Salim Tima Swale and 132 others and ordered that the status quo on L.R. No. 13061, in the Hindi/Manda Magogoni area, be maintained until October 14, 2026. The order bars the respondents from clearing, excavating, fencing, demolishing, constructing on, transferring, disposing of, or otherwise interfering with portions occupied by the petitioners. The 133 petitioners say they are long-standing occupants, cultivators and farmers with homes, crops and trees, and that their interests arise from occupation and use, not only from formal registration, and should be recognised in any compulsory acquisition. They had asked the court to restrain the Office of the President, Dangote Industries, the Lamu County Government and other respondents from a groundbreaking ceremony scheduled for Wednesday, September 30, 2026. The orders stay in force pending further directions. Source: [allafrica.com](https://allafrica.com/stories/202609290058.html)

**About 100 Israeli settlers rioted in West Bank, blocking IDF effort to allow Palestinians back home: Haaretz**
About 100 Israeli settlers rioted in the West Bank and blocked an army effort to allow a Palestinian family to return home, Haaretz reports. Settlers set fire to structures and vehicles, threw stones and wounded three Israeli officers. Three were arrested. The Palestinian family living there had suffered continuous harassment by settlers, and a court had ordered the military to secure their return. Source: [haaretz.com](https://www.haaretz.com/west-bank/2026-09-29/ty-article/.premium/idf-100-settlers-rioted-in-w-bank-thwarting-operation-to-return-palestinians/000001a0-eb9b-dbd2-affb-ebfbc7c50000)

### Also Today
**South Africa's defence giant takes $122 million artillery upgrade to Oman, with deliveries running to 2030: Business Insider Africa**
Denel is carrying out an artillery upgrade for Oman worth more than 2 billion rand, about 122 million dollars, covering the 155mm G6 wheeled system, with an upgrade facility in Oman and phased deliveries through June 2030. Source: [africa.businessinsider.com](https://africa.businessinsider.com/local/markets/south-africas-defence-giant-takes-dollar122-million-artillery-upgrade-to-oman-with/hw53wgs)

**Zimbabwe: Kariba Residents Drag Govt to Court Over Ferry Crisis After 97 Die in Mbuya Nehanda Disaster: AllAfrica**
Two Kariba residents have asked the High Court to order the government to provide adequate, safe and reliable ferries on Lake Kariba, weeks after the Mbuya Nehanda ferry disaster that claimed 97 lives. Source: [allafrica.com](https://allafrica.com/stories/202609290055.html)

**Nigeria: Resident Doctors Give Govt 14-Day Ultimatum to Meet Demands or Face Industrial Action: AllAfrica**
Nigeria's resident doctors have given the government 14 days to meet welfare and professional demands or face industrial action, citing delays despite earlier government engagements and commitments, Premium Times reported. Source: [allafrica.com](https://allafrica.com/stories/202609290042.html)

**AFCON qualifiers: Wissa guides DR Congo to win, Tunisia held by Botswana: Al Jazeera**
Yoane Wissa scored and set up the second goal as the Democratic Republic of the Congo beat Zimbabwe 2-1 in Harare in a 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier, putting DR Congo top of Group E on six points. Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/9/29/africa-cup-of-nations-qualifying-afcon-wissa-dr-congo-tunisia?traffic_source=rss)

### The Region and the World
**FAO urges more funding for Sudan as El Niño threatens food security in the region: China Daily**
The Food and Agriculture Organization is urging more money for agriculture and emergency food production in Sudan, where needs far outstrip available funding, director Rein Paulsen told China Daily in Nairobi after visiting Sudan last week. FAO is concentrating on staple crops, livestock health and animal feed; Paulsen said a programme costing about 17 million dollars last year generated more than 500 million dollars' worth of sorghum and about 22 percent of Sudan's national sorghum production. A nationwide livestock vaccination campaign is under way, with feed concentrates and mineral supplements, and Paulsen called for irrigation to be rebuilt so farmers depend less on unreliable rain. He described the anticipated El Niño as a food-security risk multiplier across the Horn. In Sudan, FAO expects rainfall significantly below normal, potentially by 30 to 40 percent, and possibly at times unsuitable for planting; in Somalia the concern is excessive rain and flooding in the Jubba and Shabelle basins. Source: [global.chinadaily.com.cn](https://global.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202609/29/WS6abb5a18e4b06d4aa0560cb0.html)

### Both Sides: Whether Serbia's court deposit is enough after extraditing a Bahraini asylum seeker
Ahmed Jaafar Mohamed Ali has been in Bahrain's Jau Prison since January 2022, after Serbia extradited him while he was seeking asylum. The Council of Europe's Committee of Ministers is pressing Serbia to carry out a March 2025 European Court of Human Rights judgment. What is being decided is whether placing the damages in a domestic account discharges Serbia, or whether Belgrade must still act so the money reaches Ali and his situation after extradition is faced.

The case for further action is put by the Committee of Ministers and by Sayed Ahmed Alwadaei, director of advocacy at the Bahrain Institute for Rights and Democracy. The court held that Serbia violated Article 3 of the European Convention on Human Rights, which bars torture and inhuman or degrading treatment, by extraditing Ali in defiance of an interim measure and without examining his complaint that he would face ill-treatment in Bahrain. The committee says Serbia should cooperate with Ali's representatives and the Secretariat so the 9,800 euro award, plus any tax and default interest, can be released without delay. Alwadaei says Serbia cannot take Bahrain's assurances at face value and must do what it can to protect Ali. Ali, in an account Middle East Eye says came from a recent call, describes beatings, an overcrowded cell in Building Two, hunger strikes and solitary confinement. His lawyers say the Interpol red notice used to arrest him in November 2021 was unlawfully issued. Campaigners say a private plane chartered by UAE-based Royal Jet took him to Bahrain three days after the interim measure.

The step Serbia has taken, as the committee records it, is that a sum for Ali has been placed in a deposit account in a domestic court. The committee also records the lawyers' point that releasing those funds is difficult because of Ali's situation in Jau Prison. He is held there on two life sentences. He fled Bahrain in 2011, lived in Iran, and travelled to Serbia to seek asylum.

Both records accept the January 2022 extradition, the two life sentences, the March 2025 finding against Serbia, and the 9,800 euro award. The committee's stated next step is cooperation so the funds can be released without delay. Source: [middleeasteye.net](https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/council-of-europe-serbia-implement-judgement-bahrain-political-prisoner)

### Progress Watch
**Sudan: Cholera cases decline after humanitarians step up support to contain outbreak: Africa.com**
Cholera cases in Sudan have declined after humanitarians stepped up support to contain the outbreak, according to a report carried by Africa.com. Source: [africa.com](https://www.africa.com/apo/sudan-cholera-cases-decline-after-humanitarians-step-up-support-to-contain-outbreak)

# Omni View Africa & Middle East
> **Seven hundred thousand barrels a day is planned for Lamu, a refinery meant to supply East Africa.**

**What You Need to Know:** Seven hundred thousand barrels a day is the planned capacity of an oil refinery Dangote Petroleum Refinery expects to start building in Lamu, Kenya, on September 30, as its entry into the East African market. Kenyan President William Ruto, visiting the group's refinery near Lagos, called that plant a masterpiece and said his government supports the group's goal. Aliko Dangote says the wider Vision 2030 plan is nearly $50 billion of industrial investment across Africa.

### Lead
**Kenyan President Ruto Calls Dangote Refinery an Engineering Masterpiece: UA.NEWS**
Kenyan President William Ruto, visiting the Dangote refinery near Lagos with his wife, Rachel Ruto, called the facility a masterpiece of science, engineering and art, and said he knew Nigerians' entrepreneurial spirit but had not expected a project of that scale. He said the Kenyan government fully supports this goal of Dangote Group. Aliko Dangote, president and chief executive of Dangote Industries Limited, said that under the group's Vision 2030 strategy it plans to invest nearly $50 billion in Africa's industrialization, including a power plant in Lamu of about 1,000 megawatts, with 500 megawatts to be sold to the Kenyan government. Dangote Petroleum Refinery expects to begin construction of an oil refinery in coastal Lamu on September 30, with a planned capacity of 700,000 barrels a day, as its entry into the East African market and a contribution to the region's energy security. Estimates cited by the outlet put construction at three years and $15 billion to $16 billion, processing oil for Kenya, South Sudan, Uganda, Burundi and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. In August, presidential economic adviser David Ndii said Dangote Group had offered East African countries a 30 percent stake, with Kenya able to take 10 percent for $500 million and Ethiopia and Rwanda ready to join; Engineers India Limited, under India's Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, is to consult on project management, engineering, procurement and construction management under a contract valued at $450 million. A mix of internal funds, an initial public offering and bonds is being considered to finance the project. Source: [ua.news](https://ua.news/en/world/prezident-keniyi-ruto-nazvav-npz-dangote-shedevrom-inzheneriyi-premium-times-nigeria)

### Across the Region
**Oil prices spike after Trump rejects Iran proposal: Middle East Eye**
Oil prices spiked, with bond yields, early Monday after US President Donald Trump rejected an Iranian offer of a seven-day truce, and Brent is back above $106 a barrel. Prices had fallen on Friday amid news of that proposal and optimism after the UN General Assembly. Trump told Axios he expects negotiations to resume, and said Tehran "overplayed their hand." He said, "They want to make a deal, but it is not the deal that I want to make...

**Somalia parliament speaker plans to cut pay of absent lawmakers: Somali Guardian**
Somalia's parliament speaker, Abdulkadir Mohamed Nur Jama, plans to cut the salaries of about 50 lawmakers for not regularly attending assembly meetings, Somali Stream reported on Sunday. He has ordered the parliament secretariat to give him the names of lawmakers often absent, and has ordered that they receive no stipends or salaries by September. If carried out, it would be the first time a speaker of the Somali parliament has made such an attempt, and the first move of this kind since his recent election. The plan would affect at least 50 lawmakers, among them ministers in the government of Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre. Source: [somaliguardian.com](https://www.somaliguardian.com/news/somalia-news/somalia-parliament-speaker-cut-pay-absent-lawmakers/)

### Also Today
**Sudan's army announces repelling Rapid Support drones in El Obeid and bombards their positions in Nyala.: CGTN**
Sudan's army says it repelled Rapid Support Forces drones in El Obeid and bombarded their positions in Nyala. Source: [news.cgtn.com](https://news.cgtn.com/news/2026-09-28/news-1QNW97CvGY8/p.html)

**South African police: death toll from weekend tavern shooting rises to 18: Reuters**
South African police say the death toll from a weekend tavern shooting has risen to 18. Source: [reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/south-african-police-death-toll-weekend-tavern-shooting-rises-18-2026-09-28/)

**Sudan’s refugee exodus to Chad jumps 20-fold as aid dries up: Middle East Online**
Sudan's refugee exodus to Chad has jumped 20-fold as aid dries up. Source: [middle-east-online.com](https://middle-east-online.com/en/sudan%E2%80%99s-refugee-exodus-chad-jumps-20-fold-aid-dries)

**Israel revokes Dutch officials' credentials over settlement goods ban: UPI**
Israel has revoked Dutch officials' credentials over a ban on settlement goods. Source: [upi.com](https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2026/09/28/revokes-status-Netherlands-officials-West-Bank/7721790558992/)

### The Region and the World
**VP Shettima Returns To Nigeria After Leading Delegation At UNGA: Channels Television**
Vice President Kashim Shettima has returned to Nigeria after representing President Bola Ahmed Tinubu at the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, a statement on Monday by Stanley Nkwocha said; he left Abuja on September 20 to lead the delegation. He delivered Tinubu's national statement at the General Debate, renewing Nigeria's call for reform of the UN Security Council and demanding permanent African representation, fairer global financing, stronger climate support and deeper multilateral cooperation. At the Third High-Level Roundtable of the Africa Minerals Strategy Group, Tinubu urged African countries to move beyond raw mineral exports toward processing, manufacturing and value addition. At an education-financing event co-hosted by Nigeria and Italy, Shettima reaffirmed education as an investment in productivity and human capital and supported the Global Partnership for Education's $5 billion financing campaign; he also met Nigerians in the diaspora, the new leadership of the ECOWAS Commission, and UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina J. Mohammed, pressing Nigeria's positions on development financing, regional integration, economic cooperation, technology, peace and security. Source: [channelstv.com](https://www.channelstv.com/2026/09/28/vp-shettima-returns-to-nigeria-after-leading-delegation-at-unga/)

### Both Sides: Whether Sudan and Ethiopia are sponsoring each other's armed opponents
The question is whether Sudan and Ethiopia should treat one another as sponsors of armed opponents, and whether that charge goes to official talks or stands as a sovereignty warning. Sudan's Armed Forces, in a statement late Sunday, reject the allegation that Khartoum backs Ethiopian opposition groups. Their strongest reason is the one they put first: Sudan, they say, stays committed to international law and to non-interference in other nations' affairs. The army says it will not permit any threat to its sovereignty or national security, and alleges that backing for the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces is still coming from Ethiopian soil, including training, supplies and military activity involving long-range and one-way attack drones. It calls on Addis Ababa to settle the differences through dialogue and official channels, in the interest of stability in both countries and the wider region. Ethiopian National Defense Force Chief of General Staff Field Marshal Birhanu Jula had accused Sudan, Egypt and other actors of supporting groups opposed to the Ethiopian government. His strongest reason is that external actors are backing an alliance of armed and political groups, and that the Tigray People's Liberation Front and Eritrea would pose a more limited threat without that outside support. His remarks came amid renewed tensions in northern Ethiopia, where clashes have intensified between federal forces and the TPLF and allied groups. Each side's statement treats cross-border help to armed groups as a security issue between the two capitals; neither accepts the other's account of who is receiving that help. The next step Sudan names is dialogue through official channels. Source: [en.yenisafak.com](https://en.yenisafak.com/world/sudan-rejects-ethiopia-claim-it-backs-opposition-3723803)

### Progress Watch
**Middle East September Crude Exports Recover to 12.8 Million Barrels a Day, Highest Since War Began: finance.biggo**
Middle East crude exports in September recovered to 12.8 million barrels a day, the highest since the war began. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/d5ebdaba-a973-4a12-b4c0-f9c655dd46e7)

# Omni View Africa & Middle East
> **Twenty-seven people are dead after two mass shootings in South Africa.**

**What You Need to Know:** Twenty-seven people were killed and twenty-six injured in two mass shootings west of Johannesburg and in Cape Town, and police are searching for the attackers. Israel's finance minister called for a West Bank war on the model of Gaza and for annexation beyond it. Iran says it has seen an initial American reaction to its proposal but not a formal reply through mediators.

### Lead
**27 killed in two mass shootings in South Africa: UA.NEWS**
Twenty-seven people were killed and another twenty-six injured in two mass shootings west of Johannesburg and in Cape Town, UA.NEWS reports, citing Deutsche Welle and South African police. In a bar west of Johannesburg, armed men killed seventeen visitors and wounded fifteen on Saturday at about 9:30 p.m. local time, and emergency services pronounced all seventeen dead at the scene. Deutsche Welle, citing South African police, reports that the attackers searched several visitors, took their mobile phones and left in two unidentified vehicles, and that the suspects may have been armed with AK-47 assault rifles and pistols. At an entertainment venue in Lwandle, Cape Town, armed men killed ten people and wounded eleven; police said five of those killed died at the scene, and the shooting began at 1:46 a.m. Police are searching for the attackers. Source: [ua.news](https://ua.news/en/world/u-par-u-dvokh-masovikh-strilianinakh-zaginuli-27-liudei-deutsche-welle)

### Across the Region
**Smotrich calls for doing in the West Bank what Israel did in Gaza: Middle East Eye**
Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich has called on Israel to “go to war” in the West Bank and “do what we did in Gaza,” Middle East Eye reports. On a Ynet podcast he said, “I certainly have solutions,” and, “I think we need to go to war in Judea and Samaria, to do there what we did in Gaza, to dismantle the Palestinian Authority, which is a terror authority.” He also called on Israel to annex southern Lebanon and the areas of Gaza still under Israeli control. He has previously called on Israel to annex more than 80 percent of the West Bank, and his campaign for next month’s election has frequently called for a significant expansion of Israeli settlements in the West Bank. Source: [middleeasteye.net](https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/smotrich-calls-doing-west-bank-what-we-did-gaza)

**President Sheikh Mohamed holds talks with senior Uzbek official in Abu Dhabi: The National**
President Sheikh Mohamed held talks in Abu Dhabi on Saturday with Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the administration of the president of Uzbekistan, aimed at advancing ties, The National reports. They explored ways to expand cooperation in support of shared development goals. Ms Mirziyoyeva delivered Uzbekistan’s address at the UN General Assembly in New York this week, stressing that the UN should work more effectively with Central Asia and stating that Uzbekistan was committed to peace and global cooperation. The Abu Dhabi meeting was attended by Sheikh Saif bin Zayed, deputy prime minister and minister of the interior; Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohamed, deputy chairman of the Presidential Court for Special Affairs; and Sheikh Mohammed bin Hamad, adviser to the UAE president. In January 2025 the two countries formalised a strategic partnership, and Etihad Airways launched daily direct flights between Abu Dhabi and Tashkent last month; the airline said the inaugural service was sold out. Source: [thenationalnews.com](https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/uae/2026/09/27/president-sheikh-mohamed-holds-talks-with-senior-uzbek-official-in-abu-dhabi/)

### Also Today
**Ethiopia’s army promises restraint amid fears of new civil war: Al Jazeera**
Ethiopia’s army has promised restraint amid fears of a new civil war, Al Jazeera reports. Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/27/ethiopias-army-promises-restraint-amid-fears-of-new-civil-war)

**Palestinian girl wounded in Israeli fire at Jerusalem checkpoint: Middle East Eye**
Israeli forces shot at and injured a Palestinian girl early Sunday at the Qalandia military checkpoint, north of occupied Jerusalem, Wafa reported, according to Middle East Eye, while Israeli authorities imposed a one-week closure on the occupied West Bank and closed border crossings, citing the Jewish holidays. Source: [middleeasteye.net](https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/palestinian-girl-wounded-israeli-fire-jerusalem-checkpoint)

**RSF drone strike hits strategic fuel depot in central Sudan: Sudan Tribune**
A Rapid Support Forces drone strike hit a strategic fuel depot in central Sudan, Sudan Tribune reports. Source: [sudantribune.com](https://sudantribune.com/article/319309)

**Saudi Arabia and Senegal convene a ministerial water dialogue at the UN: Zawya**
Saudi Arabia and Senegal, with the Global Water Organization, convened a ministerial meeting at UN headquarters in New York on “United for Water: A Call for Collective Action,” calling for stronger collective action on water security, Zawya reports. Source: [zawya.com](https://www.zawya.com/en/press-release/events-conferences/saudi-arabia-and-senegal-in-collaboration-with-global-water-organization-convene-high-level-ministerial-dialogue-at-unga-1269037)

### The Region and the World
**Iran says it has seen an initial US reaction but not a formal reply: Middle East Eye**
Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that Tehran had seen an initial reaction from US President Donald Trump to its proposal but had yet to receive a response through mediators, Middle East Eye reports. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has said Iran no longer trusts negotiations with the United States after previous rounds of talks were followed by attacks and sanctions. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has warned it will attack US warships, even those in the Indian Ocean, if Washington launches a new war against Iran. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has thanked the governments of the United Kingdom, Turkey, Oman and the UAE for supporting Washington’s “Operation Economic Outcast,” described as a harsh economic campaign against Iran. Source: [middleeasteye.net](https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/morning-recap-169)

### Both Sides: Whether Israel should open a West Bank war before the election
Whether Israel should go to war in the West Bank, and annex land, before next month’s election is a question Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich has pressed in public. Israel’s attorney general has, separately, moved to keep one settlement step off the campaign calendar.

Smotrich’s case, made on a Ynet podcast and reported by Middle East Eye, starts from his claim that he has solutions. He said Israel should go to war in Judea and Samaria, do there what it did in Gaza, and dismantle the Palestinian Authority, which he called a terror authority. He also called for annexing southern Lebanon and the areas of Gaza still under Israeli control. He has previously urged annexation of more than 80 percent of the West Bank, and his campaign for next month’s election has often demanded a large expansion of settlements. The reason he gives is that the Authority is, in his description, a terror authority, and that the approach used in Gaza should be repeated there.

The strongest contrary step in today’s reporting is procedural. Middle East Eye reports that Israel’s attorney general ordered a one-month postponement of an E1 settlement construction tender in the West Bank so it would not be used for electioneering. That order does not, in the reporting, answer the war call; it delays a settlement tender so it cannot serve the campaign.

# Omni View Africa & Middle East
> **A seven-day Iran ceasefire offer is rejected, leaving the US port blockade in place.**

**What You Need to Know:** A seven-day Iran ceasefire offer is rejected, leaving the US port blockade in place. The Wall Street Journal, cited by Middle East Eye, reports President Trump turned down Tehran's proposal and told aides he expects to resume bombing after the November midterms, while officials describe him as reluctant to restart major combat and open to changing his mind. The offer would have reopened the Strait of Hormuz and resumed nuclear talks if the United States lifted its blockade of Iranian ports.

### Lead
**Report: Trump rejects Iran's ceasefire proposal, may resume bombing after midterms: Middle East Eye**
Yesterday Iran said it had given Washington a new proposal. Today the Wall Street Journal, in an account carried by Middle East Eye, reports that President Trump has rejected Iran's proposal for a seven-day ceasefire. He has told aides he expects to resume bombing Iran after the November midterms. Citing officials, the newspaper says he is reluctant to resume major combat operations, that his views could change, and that the midterm results could sway him. Tehran's proposal would have reopened the Strait of Hormuz and resumed nuclear talks in return for the United States lifting its blockade of Iranian ports. That blockade, the report says, is causing deep damage to Iran's economy. Source: [middleeasteye.net](https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/report-trump-rejects-irans-ceasefire-proposal-may-resume-bombing-after)

### Across the Region
**UN expands list of companies operating in West Bank settlements: Middle East Eye**
The United Nations human rights office on Friday added 61 companies to its database of firms operating in Israeli West Bank settlements, which the UN considers illegal. First released in 2020, the database now lists 214 firms, mostly from Israel, and also from 10 other countries including France, Germany, China and the United States. Newly added names include Israeli pesticides maker ADAMA, part of Chinese-owned Syngenta Group, the Israel-based real estate holding company Alony Hetz, and Spain's Salvat Logistica. Those firms did not immediately respond to a request for comment. They join companies already listed, including Expedia and Airbnb, on a database the UN human rights office describes as highly sensitive because listed firms could face boycotts or divestment over settler expansion in territory home to more than 3 million Palestinians. Source: [middleeasteye.net](https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/un-adds-61-new-israeli-companies-operating-illegal-west-bank-settlements)

**Report: Egypt's intel chief came to Israel to warn of major Hamas attack 11 days before Oct. 7: Haaretz**
Haaretz reports that The Atlantic says Egypt's intelligence chief, Abbas Kamel, arrived in Israel on the 50th anniversary of the Yom Kippur War. The visit, the report says, came 11 days before the October 7 attack.

### Also Today
**Report: Yemen's government forces regain control over Taiz areas: Middle East Eye**
Yemen's government forces say they have taken several areas and higher ground in southern Taiz, including Jabal Bazel, and Presidential Leadership Council chairman Rashad al-Alimi said they had regained the advantage and could restore control over the whole country, Al Jazeera reported via Middle East Eye. Source: [middleeasteye.net](https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/report-yemens-government-forces-regain-control-over-taiz-areas)

**Body of Indian man killed in Sharjah repatriated, consulate says: The National**
India's consulate told The National that the body of an Indian man killed in Sharjah last month was repatriated on Thursday, and Sharjah Police said suspects had been referred to prosecutors after an inquiry into a death they believe resulted from a criminal act. Source: [thenationalnews.com](https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/uae/2026/09/26/body-of-indian-man-killed-in-sharjah-repatriated-consulate-says/)

**South Africa attempts record for simultaneous barbecue: UA.NEWS**
In Pretoria on Heritage Day, organizers expected about 3,000 people at 500 grilling stations to beat a 2023 record of 2,220 simultaneous cooks, and Guinness adjudicator Paulina Sapinska said a decision could be announced the following day, UA.NEWS reported, citing Asharq Al-Awsat and the Associated Press. Source: [ua.news](https://ua.news/en/world/u-par-sprobuvali-vstanoviti-rekord-iz-odnochasnogo-barbekiu-asharq-al-awsat)

**Goodbye Uncle Sidney: South Africa Mourns a Man We All Came to Love: Good Things Guy**
Chad Nathan said Sidney Miller, known in South Africa as Uncle Sidney, has died, that the circumstances are not yet confirmed, and that a friendship which began when Miller stopped in the rain to help him had raised more than half a million rand. Source: [goodthingsguy.com](https://www.goodthingsguy.com/goodbye-uncle-sidney-miller-south-africa-mourns-a-man-we-all-came-to-love/)

### The Region and the World
**Chinese VP Han Zheng pledges to deepen ties with Ghana, Cyprus: CGTN**
Chinese Vice President Han Zheng told Ghanaian President John Dramani Mahama in New York on Friday that China is ready to steadily deepen the China-Ghana strategic partnership. The meeting was held on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly. Han said China will advance cooperation in mining, green energy, vocational training and youth development, and he asked Ghana to keep a favorable environment for Chinese firms and to use China's zero-tariff policy. Mahama said Ghana adheres to the one-China policy and wants stronger ties in trade, investment, mining and manufacturing, and more people-to-people exchanges. In a separate meeting the same day, Han told Cypriot President Nikos Christodoulides that China is also ready to deepen that strategic partnership. Source: [news.cgtn.com](https://news.cgtn.com/news/2026-09-26/Chinese-VP-Han-Zheng-pledges-to-deepen-ties-with-Ghana-Cyprus-1QKvjfjLCve/p.html)

### Both Sides: Further force after launches toward Saudi cities
The contested question is whether Saudi Arabia should answer the latest launches with further force.

Gulf Cooperation Council Secretary General Jasem Al Budaiwi called missile and drone attacks on Riyadh and Khamis Mushait a serious breach of the kingdom's sovereignty and a direct threat to civilians and regional stability. His case for a hard response is that duty to protect: he said member states fully support any measures Saudi Arabia takes to protect its security, sovereignty and territorial integrity, and he asked the international community to take a firm stance to end repeated Houthi attacks. Coalition spokesman Turki Al-Maliki said air defences shot down two drones launched toward the Riyadh area and two ballistic missiles targeting Khamis Mushait.

The Houthis' stated case is that the war is already being fought on Yemeni ground. They said on Friday that Saudi warplanes launched 14 airstrikes and missile attacks in the previous 24 hours on Taiz, Amran, Marib and Saada. Yahoo News reported that Saudi return strikes have not stopped the Houthis from seizing large stretches of territory in Yemen this month. The United Nations said the escalation has displaced more than 122,000 people, and that between 6 August and 18 September, 674 people died and 2,998 were injured.

Each side's account includes the other's fire: launches toward Saudi cities, and Saudi strikes inside Yemen. The Associated Press said it could not immediately independently verify the latest interception claim, and that no Houthi statement of responsibility had yet appeared. No article sets a date for talks. The step named now is the Council's call for an international response.

# Omni View Africa & Middle East
> **Six intercepted missiles bring French soldiers to guard Saudi Arabia's Yanbu oil port.**

**What You Need to Know:** Six intercepted missiles bring French soldiers to guard Saudi Arabia's Yanbu oil port. President Emmanuel Macron said France would send soldiers, radar and defence systems and would not join the fighting, while Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan prepare an urgent chiefs-of-staff meeting. Separate reporting covers two Israeli reservists killed in northern Gaza and an Iranian proposal on ending the war.

### Lead
**France to protect key Saudi oil terminal as Houthis step up missile attacks: South China Morning Post**

President Emmanuel Macron said Thursday that France will send soldiers, radar systems and defence systems to protect the Saudi oil port of Yanbu on the Red Sea, and that French forces will not take part in combat. Saudi Arabia said it intercepted missiles fired toward Yanbu and the city of Taif. Saudi authorities reported intercepting six ballistic missiles, while the Houthis said they launched dozens of missiles and drones on Thursday. The kingdom had issued emergency warnings for Mecca, Jeddah and Yanbu. Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry said Friday that the kingdom, Turkey and Pakistan will hold an urgent meeting of their chiefs of staff on support for Riyadh. Under the Mecca Agreement, the ministry says an attack on one party is an attack on all. The three foreign ministers have already met, condemned attacks on Mecca and other civilian sites, and reaffirmed Saudi Arabia's right to self-defense. Saudi Arabia's Grand Mufti called on the military to be ready to give their lives until the Houthis are removed from power, the state news agency said late Thursday. Source: [scmp.com](https://www.scmp.com/news/world/middle-east/article/3368772/france-protect-key-saudi-oil-terminal-houthis-step-missile-attacks)

### Across the Region
**Two reservists killed in northern Gaza as recovered IDF drone explodes: Haaretz**

Two Israeli reservists were killed in the northern Gaza Strip after an Israeli military drone crashed at an army outpost, Haaretz reports. Master Sgt. Nadav Kali, 24, from Jerusalem, and Master Sgt. Ofek Moalem, 23, picked the drone up. It then detonated. Source: [haaretz.com](https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/israel-security/2026-09-25/ty-article/.premium/no-no-no/000001a0-d614-db4b-a7a5-d676b3c10000)

**Iran says it has given Trump administration new proposal for peace talks: The Washington Post**

Iran says it has given the Trump administration a new proposal for peace talks, The Washington Post reports, and The New York Times reports Iran has proposed a seven-day plan to end the war. The National reports that Iran has hardened its position on the Strait of Hormuz and insists Washington meet its conditions before formal negotiations resume. About 80 countries have backed a call for the urgent reopening of the waterway, and diplomacy at the UN General Assembly has yet to produce a breakthrough. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told Fox News that it is America that must choose whether it wants to end the war. The United Arab Emirates has suspended all flights operated by Iranian airlines to and from the country until further notice. Source: [washingtonpost.com](https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2026/09/24/iran-says-it-has-given-trump-administration-new-proposal-peace-talks/)

### Also Today
**Ghana's aviation regulator supports entry of new carriers into domestic market: MyJoyOnline**

Ghana's Civil Aviation Authority says it is ready to admit new domestic airlines to strengthen competition and help reduce fares, and Director General Stephen Wilfred Arthur says the regulator does not set ticket prices. Source: [ua.news](https://ua.news/en/world/aviatsiinii-reguliator-gani-pidtrimav-vikhid-novikh-pereviznikiv-na-vnutrishnii-rinok-myjoyonline)

**Internet disruption seen in war-hit northern Ethiopia, web monitor says: Reuters**

A web monitor has seen an internet disruption in war-hit northern Ethiopia, Reuters reports. Source: [reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/internet-disruption-seen-war-hit-northern-ethiopia-web-monitor-says-2026-09-25/)

**Kenya to double Ethiopian power imports as domestic grid pressures mount: The Africa Report**

Kenya is to double electricity imports from Ethiopia as pressure mounts on the domestic grid, The Africa Report reports. Source: [theafricareport.com](https://www.theafricareport.com/431601/kenya-to-double-ethiopian-power-imports-as-domestic-grid-pressures-mount/)

### The Region and the World
**Colombia formally cuts ties with Iran: Middle East Eye**

Colombia's foreign ministry said Thursday that the country has formally severed diplomatic relations with Iran, with the decision taking effect on Saturday. The ministry cited national and hemispheric security concerns. It accused Iran of human rights violations and alleged links to international terrorist and narcoterrorist groups. It also cited confirmed human rights violations, attacks on countries not involved in the Middle East conflict, the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, and obstruction of International Atomic Energy Agency efforts to verify Iran's nuclear programme. The ministry said those facts had deteriorated Colombia's trust in the government in Tehran. Source: [middleeasteye.net](https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/colombia-formally-cuts-ties-iran)

### Both Sides: Whether talks wait on Washington meeting Iran's conditions

The question is whether formal negotiations to end the war, and any reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, wait until Washington meets Iran's conditions.

Iran's case, as its president states it, is that the choice sits in Washington. Masoud Pezeshkian told Fox News that America must choose whether it wants to end the war, after he was asked if it could end by the end of the year. The National reports that Tehran has hardened its position on the strait and insists Washington meet its conditions before formal negotiations resume. The Washington Post reports that Iran says it has given the Trump administration a new proposal for peace talks, and The New York Times reports that Iran has proposed a seven-day plan to end the war. The strongest reason on this side is sequence: Iranian officials are putting a proposal forward and describing an end to the fighting as America's decision, with conditions before formal talks.

The case for not waiting on that sequence comes from governments treating the closure as the emergency. The National reports that about 80 countries have backed a call for the urgent reopening of the waterway, and that diplomacy at the UN General Assembly has yet to produce a breakthrough. The United Arab Emirates has suspended all flights operated by Iranian airlines to and from the country until further notice. Colombia's foreign ministry, in cutting ties, cited the blockade of the strait, obstruction of International Atomic Energy Agency checks, attacks on countries not involved in the conflict, and human rights violations. The strongest reason on this side is that a wide group of states is asking for the waterway to reopen now, while some governments are already cutting flights and relations over the blockade and the war.

Iran's stated conditions and the eighty-country call both treat the strait as not open in the ordinary way, and both sit against talks that The National says have not broken through. The proposal is now with the Trump administration, and the Emirati suspension runs until further notice.

**Daily Maverick opens the DM168 e-edition to every registered reader for World News Day: Daily Maverick**

Daily Maverick is making the DM168 e-edition free to every registered user from Friday, 25 September 2026, for World News Day on Monday, 28 September, which is also the United Nations International Day for Universal Access to Information. Anyone who signs up with an email address can read the full weekly digital edition at no cost. South Africans vote in local government elections on 4 November. More than 1,000 newsrooms in more than 100 countries are marking the day. Co-founder Branko Brkic wrote that the right to know is real only if someone makes information easy to find, check and true. # Omni View Africa & Middle East
> **South Africa's central bank raised its repo rate by a quarter point to seven point two five percent, pushing up loan costs for borrowers.**
The unanimous decision by the Monetary Policy Committee responds to inflation projected to peak at five point seven percent in November and a zero point two percent GDP contraction in the second quarter. Headline inflation stood at four point four percent in August while services inflation reached five point one percent.

### Lead
**Economic fire — Interest rate adjustment makes for interesting braai chat: Daily Maverick**
The Monetary Policy Committee of the South African Reserve Bank voted unanimously to raise the repo rate by twenty five basis points from seven percent to seven point two five percent. The prime lending rate rose automatically from ten point five percent to ten point seven five percent. Headline inflation reached four point four percent in August while the central bank projects it will peak at five point seven percent in November. Services inflation stood at five point one percent in August. The economy contracted zero point two percent in the second quarter of twenty twenty six, prompting the bank to lower its full year GDP growth forecast to one point two percent. Market analysts viewed the move as a preventive step to anchor expectations rather than the start of a longer tightening cycle. Chief Economist Johann Els at PSG Financial Services noted the unanimous vote was more hawkish than expected. Supply side price shocks are initially inflationary but ultimately deflationary for demand and growth according to Els. The adjustment marks the second such increase since the government ended austerity measures. The decision came the day before Heritage Day when many South Africans gather for braais. Archbishop Desmond Tutu had earlier linked the day to braai celebrations which boosted retail sales. The bank cited elevated long term inflation expectations above its three percent midpoint target as a key factor. Source: [dailymaverick.co.za](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-09-24-economic-fire-interest-rate-adjustment-makes-for-interesting-braai-chat/)

### Across the Region
**CAR Rebel Commander Convicted of Crimes Against Humanity: AllAfrica**
The International Criminal Court convicted Central African Republic Seleka rebel commander Mahamat Said Abdel Kani on four counts including torture and persecution for acts during the twenty thirteen conflict. Prosecutors said Said ran a Bangui prison where suspected supporters of former president François Bozizé were beaten and held in a windowless cell beneath his office floorboards. Central African Republic Justice Minister Arnaud Djoubaye Abazène welcomed the ruling and said no victim will be left behind. The twenty thirteen seizure of power by predominantly Muslim Seleka rebels triggered opposition from mainly Christian anti Balaka militias. Detainees testified about beatings and harsh conditions in the prison. The conviction covers events from the height of the conflict that ousted President Bozizé. Source: [allafrica.com](https://allafrica.com/stories/202609240254.html)

**Drone strikes kill 10 at Sudan court and college: Business Day**
Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces carried out drone attacks on government held towns in North Kordofan state. One strike hit a crowded courtroom in Um Ruwaba on September eight and killed about ten people while injuring dozens according to Emergency Lawyers. A second strike the next day hit a college in al Obeid killing a security guard and damaging eight classrooms. The dean of the college said the entire faculty felt destroyed. A student who had taken exams the previous day described her future as destroyed. The United Nations reported that drone attacks by both sides killed more than one thousand civilians in the first half of the year. Residents described the strikes as part of a new campaign after weeks of reduced activity. The Rapid Support Forces said it does not intentionally target civilians. A hospital patient in Um Ruwaba who fled earlier bombardment distinguished between strategic and suicide drones. Source: [businessday.co.za](https://www.businessday.co.za/world/africa/2026-09-24-drone-strikes-kill-10-at-sudan-court-and-college/)

### Also Today
**'GMA is monitoring Ghana's marine space blindly’ – Miracles Aboagye: modernghana.com**
New Patriotic Party communicator Dennis Miracles Aboagye said Ghana's Vessel Traffic Management Information System has been out of operation at sites including Ada Winneba Axim Keta and Half Assini forcing reliance on a less comprehensive Skylight system. The communicator argued that the system cannot provide continuous coverage for detecting smaller vessels outside port limits. He linked the surveillance gap to increased risks of narcotics movement through Ghana's maritime domain. The Ghana Maritime Authority rejected the claim and said its systems remain operational. Aboagye maintained that the collapse of the Vessel Traffic Management Information System removed a key detection and interception layer. Source: [modernghana.com](https://www.modernghana.com/news/1530390/gma-is-monitoring-ghanas-marine-space-blindly.html)

**US Mineral Investment Could Accelerate Nigeria’s Industrial and Logistics Development: nigeriahousingmarket.com**
Nigeria and the United States signed a framework agreement for cooperation in geological data mineral development processing and infrastructure with Nigeria's Minister of Solid Minerals Development Dele Alake stating the goal is to retain more value inside the country through local processing. The agreement was signed in New York by Alake and US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau. It covers the mineral value chain from exploration through development and processing. Alake said Nigeria does not want to remain primarily an exporter of raw minerals. The pact identifies infrastructure as one area for cooperation that could stimulate demand for industrial property and logistics facilities near production areas. Source: [nigeriahousingmarket.com](https://www.nigeriahousingmarket.com/news/nigeria-us-mining-pact-industrial-logistics-property)

### The Region and the World
**Djibouti, Ethiopia and Dangote plan petroleum pipeline, Ethiopian PM says: Reuters**
Djibouti Ethiopia and the Dangote group plan a petroleum pipeline that would link Ethiopian refineries to the port of Djibouti according to Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed. The project aims to improve export routes for refined petroleum products. It would connect inland production sites to coastal facilities in Djibouti. The announcement came during regional economic discussions. Source: [reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/djibouti-ethiopia-dangote-plan-petroleum-pipeline-ethiopian-pm-says-2026-09-24/)

### Both Sides: Ghana maritime surveillance effectiveness
Ghana's opposition and the Ghana Maritime Authority disagree on whether the Vessel Traffic Management Information System remains fully operational for monitoring the country's waters. Miracles Aboagye of the New Patriotic Party argues the system has been down for months at multiple coastal sites and that reliance on the Skylight alternative leaves smaller vessels and activities outside port limits undetected increasing risks of narcotics movement. The Ghana Maritime Authority states its systems remain operational for monitoring activities within Ghana’s maritime space. Both sides accept that continuous detection capability matters for intercepting illicit consignments. The next step is continued public statements from both the authority and opposition figures without a scheduled resolution date. Aboagye specifically named sites at Ada Winneba Axim Keta and Half Assini as affected. He said the CCTV cameras at those sites were also not functioning. The authority issued a statement on September twenty three rejecting the claims of downtime.

# Omni View Africa & Middle East
> **At least 11 people were killed in a mass shooting near Durban.**

**What You Need to Know:** Gunmen killed at least 11 people in a house in KwaMakhutha, near Durban, late on Tuesday. The UK is reviewing its deal to hand the Chagos Islands to Mauritius after President Donald Trump called that deal terrible. Syria’s president, at the UN General Assembly, condemned Israeli attacks and described a year of change at home.

### What This Show Covers
You want one region, every day, told straight: what was decided, what happened, what it changes and for whom. One contested question is set out with the strongest case on each side, and the day is checked for one measurable sign of progress. That is the job — not a tour of every capital, and not a verdict.

This desk covers the African continent, the Arabian Peninsula and the Gulf, the Levant, Iran and Iraq. A story filed somewhere else is here only for a concrete consequence inside that region, and that consequence is stated first.

The brief is read by Mira, the network’s AI host. The stories are chosen and written by software from named newsrooms, and every item names its source. The one thing it will not do is take a side — every claim is attributed, and no party, government or people is praised or mocked.

The other Omni View desks and Omni View Top World News sit alongside this one.

Omni View Africa & Middle East is part of the Nerra Network, an independent, ad-free network of shows at nerranetwork.com. Listen if it is useful; nothing is being sold with the invitation.

### Lead
**11 killed in mass shooting near Durban, South Africa: BBC News Africa**
Gunmen stormed a house in the KwaMakhutha township, near the South African city of Durban, late on Tuesday and opened fire on 14 people. At least 11 people were killed in that residential building. For the people inside that house, the attack is the day’s hardest counted loss. Source: [bbc.com](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/crgjqxzl097eo)

### Across the Region
**South African police officer charged with sexual offences: BBC News Africa**
Lieutenant General Shadrack Sibiya, one of South Africa’s highest-ranking police officers, has been charged with sexual offences. He made a brief appearance at a court north-west of Johannesburg. Source: [bbc.com](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cwjdvgx77n0zo)

**Al-Sharaa condemns Israel’s attacks on Syria, calls for 1974 agreement commitment: Al Jazeera English**
Syria’s President Ahmed al-Sharaa opened his UN General Assembly speech by praising what he called Syria’s “breakthrough” over the past year. He said the country had transformed “from a crisis to an opportunity” under his leadership, which is his account of the year, not an independent finding. He condemned Israel’s attacks on Syria and called for a commitment to the 1974 agreement. Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/9/23/un-general-assembly-live-irans-pezeshkian-ukraines-zelenskyy-to-speak)

**French FM Calls for Palestinians to Hold Polls: Arab News**
France’s foreign minister has called for Palestinians to hold polls. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/arabnews/status/2102758481325359126)

### The Region and the World
**UK reviewing Chagos Islands deal after Trump criticism: BBC News Africa**
Mauritius’s agreed handover of the Chagos Islands is no longer being treated in London as settled. The UK is reviewing its deal to hand the islands to Mauritius. Defence secretary Wes Streeting confirmed the deal was being looked at after US President Donald Trump called it “terrible” at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday. Source: [bbc.com](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ck3wjy3pdwdno)

### Both Sides: The Chagos transfer
What is being decided is whether the UK goes ahead with its deal to hand the Chagos Islands to Mauritius. Defence secretary Wes Streeting has confirmed the deal is being looked at. BBC News Africa reported that the review follows US President Donald Trump, who at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday called the deal “terrible”.

The case against letting the transfer stand, as Trump made it, is that judgment. He called the deal terrible before the General Assembly. Streeting’s confirmation that the deal is being reviewed comes after that criticism. The reason Trump gave, in the words the report carries, is that the deal is terrible.

The arrangement that criticism is aimed at is the UK deal to hand the Chagos Islands to Mauritius. Streeting’s stated position is that this deal is being looked at. That review is the British official position on the record today: not a fresh defence of the transfer, and not a statement that the handover has been replaced by another plan.

The fact the criticism and the review share is that a deal exists to hand the islands to Mauritius, that the defence secretary says it is being looked at, and that Trump called it terrible at the General Assembly on Tuesday. The next step the report names is that review.
